0.0.n: Describes skills useful in real situations; な connects it to 英会話.

0.1.n: Connects 実践的 to the noun it describes.

0.2.n: Refers here to conversational English skills.

0.3.n: Marks 英会話 as the object of 身につけたい.

0.4.n: Combines with で to give the time frame for acquiring the skill.

0.5.n: Marks the time frame in which the learning is accomplished.

0.6.n: Pairs with よく to describe learning without wasting time or effort.

0.7.n: The form of よい used to describe an action; 効率よく together means efficiently.

0.8.n: Literally refers to the body; 身につける is an expression for acquiring skills.

0.9.n: Links 身 to つける in the fixed expression 身につける, meaning to acquire or master.

0.10.n: つける changes to つけたい to express desire; with 身に, it refers to gaining a skill.

0.11.n: Read かた here, this is a respectful way to refer to people.

0.12.n: Marks people who want these skills as the topic; the recommendation follows in the next line.

1.0.n: A conversational version of いろいろな, placed directly before a noun.

1.1.n: 人 added to a country name means people from that country.

1.2.n: Connects the Americans to their conversations.

1.3.n: Read なま here, it emphasizes real speech rather than textbook examples.

1.4.n: Allows 生 to describe 英会話.

1.5.n: Refers here to actual conversations used as learning material.

1.6.n: Identifies 英会話 as the object of 学ぶ.

1.7.n: The plain form comes before の, which turns the action into something that can be discussed.

1.8.n: Turns 学ぶ into a noun-like phrase meaning learning.

1.9.n: Marks the whole learning phrase as the subject of 一番です.

1.10.n: Ranks this learning approach above other options.

2.0.n: Placed before 教材 to specify the subject of the learning material.

2.1.n: The quoted title that follows names this resource.

2.3.n: An English word used as part of the resource title, not a Japanese word.

2.5.n: An English verb within the resource title.

2.7.n: This occurrence forms part of the resource title This is 英会話.

2.9.n: Marks the resource as the setting where the conversations are presented.

2.10.n: Adds topic emphasis to で, setting up what this resource offers.

3.0.n: The following number specifies how many Americans are featured.

3.1.n: 約 means approximately, and 人 counts people.

3.2.n: Links the roughly 150 Americans to their conversations.

3.3.n: Read なま; it stresses natural speech from real people.

3.4.n: Connects 生 to the noun 英会話 it describes.

3.5.n: Japanese nouns do not need a plural ending, even when referring to many conversations.

3.6.n: Marks 英会話 as the object of 紹介しています.

3.7.n: 紹介する becomes 紹介している, then polite 紹介しています; here it describes what the resource offers.

4.0.n: Combines with 欄 to refer to a video's description section.

4.1.n: Names a designated space for information; 概要欄 is the video description area.

4.2.n: Marks the description section as the place where information about the resource is provided.

4.3.n: The polite ています form indicates the resource information is available; the subject and object are omitted.

4.4.n: Connects the explanation to the request that follows, giving a gentle reason.

4.6.n: Adds warm encouragement to the request.

4.7.n: The て-form of 見る plus ください makes a polite request.

0.lit: As for people who want to acquire practical English conversation efficiently within a short period,
0.tip: 身につける means acquiring a skill so it becomes part of your abilities.

1.lit: Learning various Americans' authentic English conversations is best.
1.tip: A verb followed by の can act like a noun: 学ぶの means learning.

2.lit: In the English conversation learning material This is English Conversation,
2.tip: では combines the setting marker で with the topic marker は.

3.lit: We present authentic English conversations of about 150 Americans.
3.tip: 生の describes authentic, real-life speech here; it does not necessarily mean a live broadcast.

4.lit: Since we have introduced it in the description section, please do take a look.
4.tip: ので gives a reason for the polite request 見てください.
